rejected.title: Tower Loop Engineering Converts a Low-Potential Bacterial Laccase into a High-Potential Laccase with Tunable Catalytic Activity
rejected.reason: Protein/metalloenzyme engineering and redox-property tuning rather than development of a general preparative organic synthesis methodology.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract centers on insertion and mutation of a protein loop around the T1Cu site, tuning laccase reduction potential and catalytic efficiency for biomass valorization/bioelectrocatalysis.
rejected.challengeReason: Although the engineered enzyme may be useful as a biocatalyst, the paper does not establish a defined organic preparative transformation with substrate scope; the primary methodology is protein engineering.

rejected.title: Light‐Gated Control of Brownian Rotation by a Molecular Motor
rejected.reason: Molecular-machine dynamics/physical-organic study rather than a general preparative reaction or synthesis methodology.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract focuses on photoisomerization of an overcrowded alkene motor that gates anthracene Brownian rotation, quantified by VT-NMR and DFT.
rejected.challengeReason: The molecule itself is synthetically constructed, but the scientific advance is motion control and rotational dynamics, not a transferable synthesis method.

rejected.title: Strong Second‐Order Nonlinear Optical Activities in Chiral Hybrid Copper(I) Bromide Microplates
rejected.reason: Inorganic/hybrid photonic materials study centered on nonlinear optical properties and information encoding, outside organic-synthesis methodology scope.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract emphasizes chiral Cu(I) bromide microplates, SHG intensity, laser-damage threshold, SHG circular dichroism, and photonic tagging/decoding.
rejected.challengeReason: Preparation of the microplates is a materials synthesis step, not a broadly general organic or polymer reaction methodology.

rejected.title: Vacuum‐Induced Surface Reconstruction of Mn–Ce Oxides for Low‐Temperature Coupled Redox Catalysis
rejected.reason: Heterogeneous mixed-oxide catalyst/materials study for NOx removal and chlorobenzene oxidation, without general preparative organic substrate scope.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract centers on vacuum/O2 reconstruction of Mn–Ce oxide surfaces, oxygen activation, NH3-SCR, and pollutant chlorobenzene oxidation performance.
rejected.challengeReason: An organic molecule is oxidized, but the target is environmental redox catalysis and catalyst-material optimization rather than synthesis of organic products; it fails the Gallery's preparative-scope criterion.
